summary.text: The Appalachians are a mountain range in eastern North America, running roughly 3,300 km from central Alabama to Newfoundland.
Three distinct orogenies starting about 480 million years ago built them, making them one of the oldest surviving mountain ranges in the world.
Once about as high as today's Alps and Rockies, they were worn down by 240 million years of erosion into lower, rugged peaks.

facts.label: Highest peak
facts.value: Mount Mitchell, North Carolina, 2,037 m (6,684 ft)

facts.label: Lost relatives
facts.value: Scottish Highlands, Atlas and Scandinavian Mountains

facts.label: Countries spanned
facts.value: Parts of three, including France's Saint Pierre and Miquelon

facts.label: Appalachian Trail
facts.value: About 3,500 km, from Maine to Georgia

items.prompt: The Appalachians are far lower and more rounded than the Rockies. What best explains this?

options.label: They never rose very high to begin with
They are made of soft volcanic ash
They are much older and long worn down
Their plates are now pulling them flat

items.explain: Built from about 480 million years ago, they once rivalled the Alps and Rockies before 240 million years of erosion lowered them.

items.prompt: Geologists link the Appalachians to the Scottish Highlands across the Atlantic. Why?

options.label: Both were once one range, torn apart later
The same ice sheet carved both of them
Both rose over the same mantle hotspot
Both share an almost identical climate

items.explain: Both belonged to the Central Pangean Mountains before plate tectonics split them apart.

items.prompt: Settlers heading west from the American coast found the Appalachians hard to cross. Why?

options.label: The range had no passes lower than 2,000 m
Thick ice covered the ridges all year
Active volcanoes made the region unsafe
Its ridges and valleys run across westward routes

items.explain: The range forms alternating ridges and valleys that cut across east–west travel, a barrier that shaped colonial-era expansion.

items.prompt: Walking north along the range, how does the forest tend to change?

options.label: Maples and beech take over completely
Conifers like spruce and fir take over
Forest gives way to desert scrub
Oak and chestnut grow ever thicker

items.explain: Red spruce and balsam fir dominate the north and high ground, while sugar maple and beech are more common further south.

items.prompt: Where does the name of these mountains first come from?

options.label: A Native village in today's Florida
A Scottish word for a rocky ridge
The surname of a French mapmaker
A Dutch word for the eastern hills

items.explain: Spanish explorers recorded a village name, Apalachen, near present-day Tallahassee; it was later applied to the tribe, the region and the mountains.

items.prompt: Which industries historically drew many migrants into the Appalachian region?

options.label: Cotton farming and textiles
Fishing and whaling
Oil drilling and refining
Logging and coal mining

items.explain: The range's economy rested largely on logging and coal mining, which brought in many migrants.
